scope: Original deliberately faulty teaching fixtures. Weak suites assert exact outcomes but intentionally omit a distinguishing input. Each study names the layer that catches the mistake: native Rust type or name checking, native overflow checks, the compiled strict ABI or checked arithmetic recorded in the referenced corpus case, or none for the negative controls. These are host Rust compiler/tests and independent Chialisp/Rue VM executions plus references to executed corpus cases, not Rust-to-CLVM or consensus proofs.

studies.title: A deposit silently grows past 64 bits
studies.claim: Fixed-width u64 arithmetic compiled with overflow checks panics on the overflowing deposit natively, and the project compiler emits checked arithmetic that rejects it in CLVM; Chialisp integers grow without bound.
limitations: Native overflow behavior depends on compiler settings; this study enables overflow checks explicitly, and the corrected fixture uses checked_add so the rejection no longer depends on them.

The compiled-subset credit is the referenced corpus case, where the independent Chialisp module accepts the unbounded sum and the Rust CLVM rejects it in both optimizer modes; that is finite executed evidence, not a compiler-preservation proof.
Rue Int is unbounded by design, so the Rue translation reproduces the growth; a bounded Rue type or explicit guard would be needed.

declared_divergence.reason: Checked i64 addition overflows and rejects; the original returns the unbounded sum.

studies.title: A padded amount atom is accepted as an amount
studies.claim: The compiled strict typed ABI rejects the noncanonical amount atom before the function body runs; native Rust has no padded seven, so this is a runtime ABI rejection rather than a compiler guarantee.
limitations: Nothing in the Rust source changes between the faulty and corrected fixtures: the decoder generated for the default strict ABI performs the check, and an explicit ignored or raw environment would not.

The compiled credit is the referenced corpus case, where the independent Chialisp module reads the padded atom as an integer and the Rust CLVM rejects it in both optimizer modes; that is finite executed evidence, not a compiler-preservation proof.
Rue Int carries the padded bytes through to the condition in both optimizer modes.

corpus_evidence.case: padded atom rejects in Rust; the original reads it as one

declared_divergence.reason: The original reads any atom as a signed integer, so a padded encoding is accepted; the typed Rust ABI rejects noncanonical integer atoms.

corpus_evidence.scope: Executed corpus observation of the compiled layer; finite evidence, not a compiler-preservation proof.

studies.title: An extra solution element is silently ignored
studies.claim: A Rust signature fixes the argument count: a host caller passing a third field fails to compile, and the compiled strict ABI rejects a third solution element at runtime.
limitations: The host diagnostic concerns Rust callers; on chain the solution is attacker-controlled, so the compiled strict ABI's proper-list and arity check is the layer that matters there, as the referenced corpus case shows.
An explicit ignored or raw environment ABI would not add this check.
Positional Rue parameters ignore extra elements like Chialisp; a rest pattern with an explicit shape assertion can reject them, so this is a convention rather than a Rue type error.
